reason: The named-provider registry and the single activation manager are kept as component subagent.manager in internal/delegate/subagent. Each activation becomes a fiber under a per-tree fiber owned by the root agent's scope, the per-parent catalog becomes one tree ledger in the root's log, and settlement gets one fixed order with a durable record before anyone is told.

The ACP provider is kept as a Runner on the shared external run lifecycle: one agent process per task, started through the one spawn helper, driven by the client role of the acpwire wrapper. It gains a third permission policy, ask, that forwards the agent's permission request to a person.

Upstream drives a bundled Claude Code executable through the vendor's npm SDK. The Go provider gives the same one-shot delegation by starting the claude executable the user installed in print mode and reading its streaming JSON, as the library specification decided; the provider contract, the operator-fixed permission mode and the fixed-word diagnostics are kept.

The Codex provider keeps upstream's shape: one app-server process, one unsaved thread and one turn per task over a minimal hand-written client. The executable is the one the user installed, not a bundled one, and a fourth permission mode, ask, routes approval requests to a person.

The provider that runs a task in a second dsh process over the SDK protocol is kept on the shared external lifecycle. By default it starts the running executable, it may share the harness home because sessions are leased, and it passes preset, depth and creator at initialize.

The fork provider is kept as a Preparer that returns the creator's completed-turn prefix and never sees the child agent; it lives with spawn in internal/delegate/subagent/local. The prefix rule is protected by a test that compares the request head byte for byte.
The spawn provider is kept as a Preparer that returns an empty seed; the manager creates the child agent, applies the delegation boundary and mounts the inherited or named preset.

The delegation tool (one component per configured instance), the model discovery tool and the live route setting are kept in internal/delegate/subagent/tools. Added: several operator-declared targets behind one tool, a wait argument that returns the bounded result, preset descriptions in the schema and a composition-time check of preset ids.

send_message, wait_agent, interrupt_agent and list_agents and the identity context are kept as component subagent.tools. Listing is paged and reads one projection, a wait is keyed on the inbox's log position, and a settled child can be dismissed.

The task board and the per-session Team mode are kept as component team.board with service key team.Key: whole-task snapshots in the root's log changed by compare-and-set. Added: one change notice per task, a user as actor, and release of a task whose owner's run failed.

The four task tools and the team policy prompt section are kept as component team.tools, shown for a whole tree only while the root's Team mode is on, with the same schemas for the root and every member.
Each ACP delegation still starts one fresh agent process and pays the handshake; no pool is designed.
justification: One process per run is what lets the run own the whole process tree and prove it gone before the result is released (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-3, DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5). A pooled process would be shared between delegations and so between owners. Revisit only with a measured start-up cost.

reason: The ACP child still receives a local path and runs on the host's own machine; no remote workspace mapping exists.
justification: A remote child needs the SSH transport of area A10 and a mapping between host and remote workspace paths that no area has designed. The start request's directory is chosen by the host, so a remote provider can be added later without changing the provider contract.

reason: Reduced, not removed. An output schema is now validated by the manager for every provider, and the depth check applies to the child being started whatever the provider, so both work for an ACP child. An agent preset and harness model options still cannot be applied inside a foreign agent and are refused at admission.
justification: A preset is a composition of harness components and has no meaning inside another product; refusing the request, instead of silently dropping it, is upstream's capability rule and is kept (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5).

reason: The parent's log still receives only the agent's final text, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic. Other ACP updates are offered as the unlogged subagent.Progress event for a view.
justification: A child's working trace must not enter its creator's model context or log: results are bounded by decision DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9 and by outcome DH-O-6. The full trace belongs to the child product.

reason: The ACP provider gains the policy ask: the agent's session/request_permission is forwarded through the run's Ask callback to the interaction registry and shown to the root's answerer with the child's name. With no answerer the request is rejected, and reject stays the default policy.
One fresh Claude Code process per run, with no saved session, continuation or pool, is kept. The only addition is a live, unlogged Progress event.
justification: One process per run is what makes ownership and cleanup exact (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5), and the library decision DH-ADR-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-1 runs print mode with session persistence turned off so that nothing of the product's state is left to clean up.

reason: One delegation tool may list several operator-declared targets (alias, provider instance, description), and the model picks one with the target argument, so a call chooses among instances without one uniquely named tool per instance. The model and the permission mode of an instance stay fixed by the operator on purpose.

The provider configuration has an explicit settings field: native (the user's Claude settings apply, as upstream) or bare (the product's bare mode, which skips settings, hooks and stored logins and needs a key in env). A hermetic mode therefore exists and the choice is written down instead of implied.

The harness still does not create an account, log in or edit Claude settings. A sign-in failure is reported with its stage and, only where the product states it as a closed fact, with the category auth instead of unknown.
justification: Account state belongs to the vendor's product and to the user; managing it would mean handling another vendor's credentials, which DH-ADR-SECURITY-6 keeps out of harness configuration. The classification cannot be finer than what the product reports.

reason: No vendor payload is installed by a package manager. The provider starts the claude executable the user installed, probes it and its version before the first run, and fails a delegation with subagent/unavailable when it is missing, so the host's own program is the path and not a missing fallback.
A Claude Code child still cannot ask a person: permission prompts are denied and questions are unavailable to it.
justification: The library decision DH-ADR-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-1 drives print mode, which has no channel to answer a prompt, and gave up the SDK's callbacks. A user who needs prompts reaches Claude Code through the ACP provider with permission ask. Revisit if the vendor documents an answer channel for print mode.

reason: Only the final answer, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic enter the parent's log. The settled record adds usage when the product reports it, and a live Progress event shows activity to a view.
justification: A child's reasoning, tool traffic and stderr must not enter its creator's model context: results are bounded by decision DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9 and outcome DH-O-6, and stderr may hold secrets.

reason: Reduced, not removed. An output schema and the depth check now work for a Claude Code child because the manager applies them. A harness preset and a per-call model choice are still refused for this provider.
justification: A preset has no meaning inside another product, and the model of a product instance is fixed by the operator so that a model cannot change cost or authority (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7); a choice among instances is given by tool targets.

reason: Reduced, not removed. Every external instance has maxDuration (default one hour), which cancels the run with cause budget. Files or external systems the child changed before a cancel are still not restored.
justification: Workspace files are the user's and are classed as uncertain after a failed run (design section 5). The only real rollback is a working directory per child, which section 10 lists as not designed.

reason: One fresh Codex app-server process, one unsaved thread and one turn per run are kept, with no continuation or pool. The only addition is a live, unlogged Progress event.
justification: One process per run is what makes ownership and cleanup exact (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5), and the library decision DH-ADR-CODEX-1 keeps the unsaved thread so that nothing of the product's state is left behind.

reason: One delegation tool may list several operator-declared targets, and the model picks one with the target argument, so a call chooses among Codex instances and other providers without one uniquely named tool each. An instance's model and permission mode stay fixed by the operator on purpose.

The harness still does not create an account, log in, trust a project or edit Codex settings. A failure that the product reports with HTTP status 401 or 403 is given the category auth; anything else keeps its stage and the unknown fallback.
justification: Account and project-trust state belong to the vendor's product and to the user; managing them would mean handling another vendor's credentials (DH-ADR-SECURITY-6). The classification cannot be finer than what the product reports.

reason: No native payload is installed by a package manager. The provider starts the codex executable the user installed, probes its version before the first run, and fails a delegation with subagent/unavailable when it is missing.

The exact-version pin is replaced by a minimum version, a tested range, and a real-product scenario that asks the installed Codex for its protocol schema and checks the fields the client relies on. An unknown server request, phase or terminal status fails closed. Each new Codex release still has to be proven by running that scenario.

A fourth permission mode, ask, takes the approval requests that upstream's client declines and forwards them through the run's Ask callback to the interaction registry and the root's answerer. With no answerer, and for an unknown request, the answer is still no. The default mode stays never.
Only the selected answer, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic enter the parent's log. The settled record adds usage when the product reports it, and a live Progress event shows activity to a view.
justification: A child's reasoning, tool traffic and stderr must not enter its creator's model context: results are bounded by decision DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9 and outcome DH-O-6.

reason: Reduced, not removed. An output schema and the depth check now work for a Codex child because the manager applies them. A harness preset and a per-call model choice are still refused for this provider.
justification: A preset has no meaning inside another product, and the model of a product instance is fixed by the operator so that a model cannot change cost or authority (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7); a choice among instances is given by tool targets.

reason: Reduced, not removed. Every external instance has maxDuration (default one hour), which cancels the run with cause budget. Files or external systems the child changed before a cancel are still not restored.
justification: Workspace files are the user's and are classed as uncertain after a failed run (design section 5). The only real rollback is a working directory per child, which section 10 lists as not designed.

reason: Each SDK delegation still starts one fresh dsh runtime, which boots a whole component tree; there is no pool.
justification: One process per run is what makes ownership and cleanup exact (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5). A Go binary starts faster than a Node runtime, and a task that does not need process isolation uses the in-process providers.

reason: The child is the same binary, so the parent passes the preset id, the delegation depth and its creator in the SDK initialize call and the child host applies them; an output schema is validated by the parent's manager. This needs those initialize fields from area A20.

The provider's home may be set to same, which DH-ADR-12 makes safe: the child host writes its session into the parent's database under its own lease with the delegating agent as creator, so the child's transcript is listed and opened like any other child session.
The SDK child still runs as a local process in a local directory; a remote runtime is not designed.
justification: A remote child needs the SSH transport of area A10 and a mapping between host and remote workspace paths that no area has designed. The start request's directory is chosen by the host, so a remote provider can be added later without changing the provider contract.

reason: A fork child still sees its creator's completed turns as of the fork and nothing the creator logs later.
justification: A session is an independent append-only log (DH-O-4): sharing later context live would put text into the child's requests that its own log could not rebuild. A creator that wants to share more sends a message.

reason: Two of the four named causes cannot arise in Go: there is no generated SDK and no restored historical override. Structured output no longer adds a child-only tool, because the manager validates the final answer. An explicit route change stays the caller's choice. A test asserts that a fork child's first request has its creator's system prompt and tool schemas byte for byte.
Shipped fork tools still offer no model route fields.
justification: A provider's prefix cache is keyed by model, so a fork on another model can never reuse the inherited prefix that fork exists for. The fields stay off by default and an operator may turn them on, as upstream.

reason: A spawn child still starts with none of its creator's conversation.
justification: That is this provider's contract: the fork provider exists for the other case, and the tool description says which of the two the model is calling. Merging them would make every delegation pay for the inherited history.

reason: The whole tree is one projection folded from the root's log, so listing descendants is one read and needs no observation per member; a cold root needs one fold from its projection checkpoint.
A name still cannot be changed or reused once its child was published. The part about children that predate names does not arise, because the Go store reads no upstream session.
justification: A name appears in logged messages, notices and task owner fields; reusing it would make that history ambiguous. A start that never published frees its name, and dismissal removes a child from listings (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-4).

reason: ACP, SDK, Codex and Claude Code children still run once and accept no follow-up; their ledger records stay readable after the run.
justification: Each external run is one process that the run owns and stops. A follow-up needs the product to keep and reopen a conversation, which the library decisions turn off on purpose (no saved session, an unsaved thread). The Continuable capability lets a later provider offer it without a contract change.

reason: A model-authored message still stays within one tree and reaches only the root or a local member; a person keeps a separate prompt path with a queue-or-steer choice.
justification: Tree membership is the only authority for a model-authored message (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-8). Crossing trees needs an address book and a new authorisation input that no consumer asks for; a person can prompt any session they may access.

reason: The agent contract of area A02 queues a waking send that arrives while a turn is being cancelled as a new turn, so nothing stays parked waiting for a second send. The manager's Send and Interrupt use that contract unchanged; the dependency on A02 is stated in section 10.

Settlement looks only at waking input. Injected context that is parked stays in the logged inbox and is restored when the child is next resumed, so it no longer has to keep the child, or its creators, in memory.

The session lease of DH-ADR-12 makes a tree belong to the one process that holds the root's lease. A second process that opens a member is refused with subagent/busy-elsewhere, and slots are counted in that one process. Nothing is delivered across processes, and a single writer needs no such delivery.

Accepting a message means its inbox splice is committed: Send returns the durable receipt of area A02, so an accepted prompt is in the child's log before the sender is told. A start is likewise recorded and flushed before anything is created.

A start passes the around event subagent.Admit, where a policy component returns Allow or Deny with a reason. Keeping a child running at its end uses the child's own TurnStopping point of area A02, which a listener on the tree's root can reach because tree events are dispatched through the root's scope.
send_message still returns a receipt and never the target's reply.
justification: A reply cannot be attributed to one message once steering lets several messages share a step; area A02 fixes that a send returns a receipt. A reply is another message, and a caller that wants a return value starts a child with wait.

reason: A member cannot be live without its root, because every activation is a fiber under the root's tree fiber. For a cold target the host resumes the root first and then only the target, so a missing root is repaired instead of reported. External and dismissed targets still cannot receive messages.

Only the holder of the root's lease can activate a member, so one projection snapshot plus that process's live registry cannot disagree with another process. A listing is still a snapshot in time; interrupt and send check authority themselves.
A wait remembers the inbox's log position it last reported, not message ids. Replacing a pending message is a new splice at a later position, so it ends the next wait.
list_agents takes a cursor and a limit (default 50, at most 200), and Dismiss removes a settled child from listings and from messaging by a ledger record without deleting its session.

The delegation tool takes wait: true. The call then blocks until settlement and returns the bounded result with caller delivery, and cancelling the call disposes the child. This is also what a workflow script calls through the tool command line.

The agent_preset choice lists each allowed preset with its description. The tool set is resolved once per step in Go, so reading descriptions at that point does not depend on declaration order. It needs a description field on presets from area A27.

Preset ids in a tool's configuration are checked against the composed preset ids when the layers are composed and again at each reload, so a misspelling is a diagnostic with file and line. The id is still resolved again at delegation.
Shipped fork tools still leave model selection off.
justification: A provider's prefix cache is keyed by model, so a fork on another model can never reuse the inherited prefix that fork exists for. The option stays off by default and an operator may turn it on under the same route authorisation, as upstream.

reason: The depth cap is a value resolved at each delegation (the tool instance's live field, else the host setting), and the check applies to every provider. A different cap is a configuration edit that takes effect at the next call, not a second tool, and provider-managed is dropped.
A task change publishes one team.TaskChanged notice that names the task and its revision, and the server-rendered board swaps that one row. The whole board is never broadcast. The view is area C5's.
Members still share one checkout; there is no worktree, remote member, merge or file lock.
justification: The shared checkout is upstream's stated boundary, and isolation is a product decision nobody has made. A worktree as an activation effect is sketched in docs/usage.md and listed as not designed in section 10; the host-chosen directory of a start lets it be added without a contract change.

reason: Write scopes still only warn; a shell command, a formatter or a generator can write outside them.
justification: Confinement is the sandbox's job (area A10). Mapping a member's scopes to sandbox write roots is listed as not designed in section 10, and it would hold only where a backend reports full enforcement.

reason: There are no task notices to miss: by decision a task change wakes nobody, an agent that must act is sent a message, and a message resumes a cold member. A settlement notice for a member that was away is derived from the ledger when it is next resumed.
Members still cannot message another team, and only an ancestor or the user can interrupt a member.
justification: Tree membership is the only authority for a model-authored message, and ancestry the only one for a model-requested stop (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-8). Crossing trees needs an authorisation input that no consumer asks for.

reason: A member's activation is a fiber under its root's tree fiber, so a member cannot be live while its root is gone, and a cold member is reached by resuming the root first. A member therefore always has an active team.

When the ledger shows that a task owner's latest run settled as anything but completed, or that the owner was dismissed, the board appends a release revision that names the cause; the same rule runs when the root is resumed after a crash. An owner that is merely inactive keeps its task, and task views say whether the owner is resident.

The team/message/queued and team/message/delivered records exist upstream only so that session logs written by earlier upstream releases stay readable in Node. The Go design has no team mailbox type and its store reads no upstream session (DH-ADR-2, DH-ADR-11), so there is no historical message to leave undelivered.
The team policy text still coordinates and does not confine: it cannot stop a shell command or an external process from writing overlapping files.
justification: Confinement is the sandbox's job (area A10), not a prompt's. Enforcing write scopes as sandbox write roots is listed as not designed in section 10.

reason: A live member always has a live root, because its activation is a fiber under the root's tree fiber. A task call still checks mode and authority again under the board's mutex when it runs, so a tool that was visible at step start cannot act after Team mode was turned off.

The Board interface takes an actor that is an agent or an owner principal, so the web board of area C5 can create, edit, reassign and release tasks through the same compare-and-set commands the tools use.

The final answer of a local child is read backwards from the end of its log and stops at the first non-empty assistant message after the run's start; the text-stream fallback is folded only when no such message exists. The whole suffix is never folded at settlement.

title: A child that delegates and then ends its turn settles before its own children, and their completion notices are dropped because their creator is no longer online, although the delegation guidance tells the model to end its turn while it waits

reason: A local child does not settle while a child it created with parent delivery is unsettled; the notice then wakes it, so the end-turn guidance is true at every depth. A result that still finds no resident creator is in the ledger and is delivered when that creator resumes.

The Go harness exposes the same delegation tool under each instance's configured name, with description, prompt and optional name. It adds target (several operator-declared providers behind one tool) and wait (return the bounded result instead of a notice); route and preset fields stay optional and authorised.
The Go harness exposes the same discovery tool, reading the live host route setting at each call; its result is paged at 100 rows.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same two arguments. It steers the target, resumes a cold local member, and returns the durable receipt; the message size is bounded by maxMessageBytes.

The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same timeout range and the same one-field result. It observes only the caller's next-step inbox and is keyed on the inbox's log position, so an edited message ends a wait.

The Go harness exposes the same tool: an ancestor asks a descendant to stop its current work, a local target keeps its queue, an external run stops for good, and an absent target is an accepted no-op.

The Go harness exposes the tool with a changed schema: optional cursor, limit and include_dismissed, and the statuses running, inactive, settled and missing. It reads one ledger projection instead of one catalog per member.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same arguments (subject, description, blocked_by, write_scopes), shown only while the root's Team mode is on.
The Go harness exposes the same tool; the task view adds whether the owner is resident.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same filters and the same page limit of 100.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with the same eight actions and the required expected_revision; a stale revision returns the current one and only the root reassigns.
Replaced by the typed notify event subagent.Started, dispatched through the tree root's scope after the start record is durable and the task accepted, so a listener on the root sees its whole tree.

Replaced by the typed notify event subagent.Settled, dispatched through the same scope after cleanup and after the settled record is in the root's log; it carries the stop reason, the cleanup state and the record's sequence number.

Folded with provider-removed into one typed notify event, subagent.ProvidersChanged, with a name and an added flag. The delegation tool no longer listens: tool visibility is resolved per step from the registry.

Folded with provider-added into one typed notify event, subagent.ProvidersChanged, with a name and an added flag. Removing a provider blocks new starts and stops that provider's external runs with it.
Replaced by the Go struct subagent.Config: maxActive (8) and maxDepth (1) as upstream, plus maxStartsPerTree (200), noticeMaxBytes (32768) and childApprovals (ask-root or deny); every field is live.
Replaced by the Go struct local.SpawnConfig with the one field name (default spawn).
Replaced by the Go struct local.ForkConfig with the one field name (default fork).

Replaced by the Go struct sdkchild.Config: name, binary (default the running executable), profile, layers, home (required, same or an absolute path), model, env, maxDuration and stopGrace. The three separate timeouts of upstream become one stop ladder from the spawn helper.
Replaced by the Go struct acp.Config: name, command (required), args, permission (reject, allow or ask), env, maxDuration and stopGrace.
Replaced by the Go struct claudecode.Config: name, executable (default from PATH), model, permissionMode (default dontAsk), settings (native or bare), env, maxDuration and stopGrace.
Replaced by the Go struct codex.Config: name, executable, model, permissionMode (never, approve-for-me, ask or the bypass mode), env, maxDuration and stopGrace.

Replaced by the Go struct tools.DelegateConfig: tool, provider or targets, modelSelection, modelDiscovery, model, preset, allowedPresets and maxDepth. The value provider-managed is dropped, and removed keys need no special rejection because decoding is strict.
Replaced by the Go struct tools.ControlConfig: interrupt (default true), plus listLimit (50) and maxMessageBytes (65536).
Replaced by the Go struct team.Config: maxTasks (256) and defaultEnabled (false) as upstream, plus releaseOnOwnerFailure (true).
The component team.tools takes no configuration, as upstream; with strict decoding any key in its entry is a load error, which replaces upstream's start-up warning for removed keys.

Replaced by service key subagent.Key with interface Runtime: Register, Start, Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Dismiss, Tree, Resolve, RootOf and WaitQuiet. drainDescendants has no counterpart because root teardown is structural.
Replaced by service key subagent.RoutesKey, whose Allowed method reads the live host setting subagent-model-selection at every call and returns the authorised routes or that selection is off.
Replaced by service key team.Key with interface Board: Mode, SetMode, Create, Get, List and Update, each taking an actor that is an agent or an owner principal.

Kept: a fork child has its creator's tool list and prompt head and receives its task after the inherited history. Go removes two of the note's listed ways to break the prefix (no generated SDK, no restored overrides) and one more by validating structured output in the manager instead of adding a child-only tool; a test compares the request head byte for byte.
summary: A forked child keeps its parent's tool list and system prompt prefix and gets its task after the inherited history, so the provider can reuse the cached prefix.

reason: Kept: one send_message operation in every direction, always delivered as a steer, with one durable source that names the sender, and no separate report tool. The receipt is durable in Go because the inbox is a logged queue.
summary: Agents use one send_message operation in both directions; it always steers the target and records one durable sender attribution.

reason: The note's aim is kept: the creation fact is recorded where it is known, and nothing scans all sessions. Its mechanism changes. When the note was written a parent owned its children; upstream later moved runtime ownership to the tree root. Go therefore keeps one ledger of starts and settlements in the root's log, which lists a tree in one read, holds the outcome that the catalog lacks, and still ignores records inherited through a fork.
summary: Each parent session records its direct children in its own catalog events, which are the authority for finding children.

reason: Kept: an agent's own name, its creator's and the root's are required runtime context derived from the live tree at each request, so identity survives compaction and is right after an ordinary fork. The control-tool component contributes it; it needs required context entries from area A03.
summary: A subagent's identity is supplied as required runtime context derived from the live tree, not written into its first task message.

reason: Kept: a teammate is an ordinary subagent identified by its session id, there is no roster, and every root with its descendants is the team. The team component adds only the board and its policy text.
summary: A team member is an ordinary subagent; there is no separate roster, and the team feature adds only tasks and task policy.

reason: Kept: listing and messaging span the whole tree, the sender must be a live member of it, delivery re-checks that, only the target is resumed, and the root owns runtime instances while creators keep the lineage. Go makes the root's ownership structural: activations are fibers under a tree fiber of the root's scope.
summary: Listing and messaging work across the whole subagent tree under one root, with authority from tree membership.

reason: Kept: the team owns task storage, dependencies and compare-and-set commands only; identity, discovery, messaging, interruption and waiting are the ordinary subagent tools; no task notice is written into any inbox.
summary: The team feature owns only tasks; everything else comes from the ordinary subagent tools, and task state lives in the task journal.

reason: Kept: Team mode is a saved choice on the root session, default off, read by the whole tree; turning it off keeps tasks and children; a deployment default is applied once at creation and never at resume. The profile migration the note describes has no Go counterpart.
summary: Team mode is a saved per-session choice on the root, default off, not a switch in the shared profile.

reason: Kept: a user prompt or interrupt names only the child session, that session is the access resource, and access to a parent does not imply access to a child. Extended: the host resumes the root first when it is not resident, so the note's requirement of an already live root is no longer an error path.
summary: A user prompt or interruption for a subagent addresses only that child session, which is its access resource.

reason: Kept: the control-tool component owns the guidance about reporting to the delegating agent and emits it as runtime context only when its tool is visible in the step; the manager owns result delivery and promises a notice only for parent delivery.
summary: The messaging tool component owns the reporting guidance and emits it only when its tool is available; the manager owns result delivery.

reason: Kept: the same name rule, the default agent-N, paths from the root with lead for the root, synchronous reservation, and the session id as the only execution identity. The name is now a field of the start record in the root's ledger, and a start that never published frees its name.
summary: Each child gets a short name unique among its creator's children; the session id stays the only identity.

reason: Kept: the sentence that tells the model to end its turn instead of sleeping stays in the delegation guidance unchanged. Go also makes it true below the root, where upstream releases a child that follows it before its own children report: a creator that is owed results stays resident and is woken by the notice.
summary: The delegation guidance keeps the sentence telling the model to end its turn when only waiting for subagent results remains.

reason: Kept: a tool instance registers once in the composition that owns it and agents on that preset inherit it. Changed in one point: the note accepts that an unknown preset id is found only when selected; Go checks preset ids when layers are composed and still resolves the id again at delegation.
summary: Each delegation tool instance registers once in the composition that owns it; agents sharing a preset revision inherit it.

reason: The depth policy is kept and widened: an absolute cap checked at each start with the tool still visible, now applied by the manager for every provider, so the provider capability and the value provider-managed disappear. The persona and tool-filter half of the note exists only to restore children written by earlier upstream releases, which the Go store does not read (DH-ADR-2).
summary: maxDepth is an absolute cap on delegation depth; persona and tool-filter overrides are restored only for historical children.

reason: Kept: a continuable child is one durable session with at most one live activation, the agent's own inbox is the only queue, a local provider contributes only creation data, cold resume does not go through a provider, and a caller's cancellation owns work only until inbox acceptance. The direct-parent rules the note itself marks as superseded are not carried.
summary: A continuable subagent is one durable session with at most one live activation; the agent's own inbox is the only turn queue.

reason: Kept: a board of whole-task snapshots with monotonic revisions, compare-and-set on every mutation, a dependency graph without cycles, advisory write scopes, root-only reassignment, and the split into a domain service and a tool component. Changed in one point: the note leaves a failed owner on its task; Go releases the task by a recorded revision.
summary: Every root session and its descendants form a team with a durable compare-and-set task board, split into a domain service and a tool package.

reason: Kept: each product provider has a permission mode in its own vocabulary, fixed per instance by the operator, with safe defaults that never ask and no permission field in the tool schema or the start request; diagnostics are fixed words capped at 4096 bytes. Extended: Codex gets an ask mode that routes approval requests to a person, because its protocol has an answer channel; Claude Code's print mode has none.
summary: Claude Code and Codex providers run unattended with a permission mode fixed in the deployment profile; the model cannot change it.

reason: Kept: a host setting holds an enabled switch and a list of exact provider and model routes; a new adapter or model never widens it; with the setting off only the creator's current route is allowed; discovery and delegation check the same list; fork tools leave route fields off.
summary: A host setting stores the exact model routes a parent may choose for a child; registering a model never widens the list.

reason: The semantics are kept: an explicit preset mounts the currently registered definition even when it equals the creator's, omission joins the creator's live composition, and a missing saved preset fails restoration. The mechanism changes: upstream tells the two cases apart by the order of two events so that older logs keep working; Go records the selection in the Preset field of the child's session header.
summary: An explicit spawn preset resolves the current definition; omission joins the parent's composition; an event ordering marks which on restore.

reason: The proposal was never built upstream. Its three mechanics already exist in this design: a fork at the last completed turn is the fork provider, a result that goes to the caller and not to the parent is caller delivery, and the advisor framing and the merged note are injected context of area A02. No new mechanism or deliverable is added; a user-facing command and its view are left to areas A17 and C5.
summary: Proposal, not built: a side session forked at the last completed turn acts as a read-only advisor and can merge one note back.

reason: Kept: the route list is read from the live setting at each delegation and discovery call, so an edit applies to the next call in every session, and an invalid enabled setting fails the call that reads it and not agent creation. The retired session event the note keeps declared has no Go type.
summary: The models a subagent may be routed to are read from the live setting at each call, not copied into each session.

reason: Kept: one entry point for every provider, a handle with the child's identity, a result that settles only after cleanup, disposal of exactly that activation, and a captured result that survives a cleanup failure. Go adds what the note says external children lack, a durable record of the outcome, and replaces the child-only structured-output tool by validation in the manager.
summary: Every way of running a subagent goes through one entry point that returns a handle whose result settles only after cleanup.

reason: Kept: a child's persona and tools come from the preset it selects or inherits, and fork cannot replace them. The explicit rejection of removed keys needs no code in Go because configuration is decoded strictly, and the parsing kept for older child descriptors is not needed (DH-ADR-2).
summary: A subagent's persona and tool set come from its agent preset, not from separate settings on the subagent tool.

reason: Kept: wait_agent ends only on input in its caller's own next-step inbox, on timeout or on cancellation; queued next-turn input, other agents' activity and task changes do not end it. Go keys the wait on the inbox's log position, which also ends it when a reported message is edited.
summary: wait_agent ends only when a message arrives in its caller's own inbox, or on timeout or cancellation.

reason: Kept: the team projection holds only tasks and the saved mode. The other half of the note, ignoring older member and mailbox records, has nothing to ignore in Go because those event types are not registered and upstream logs are not read (DH-ADR-2).
summary: The team state derived from the log holds only the task list and the saved mode.

title: One manager; an activation is a fiber in a tree the root owns; lineage is data

A result settles in one fixed order, is durable before anyone is told, and a creator owed results stays resident
Three bounds, refused and never queued; names are held by the ledger
Two provider shapes, declared capabilities, and one run lifecycle for every external provider
Session grants never cross the delegation boundary; a child asks the root's answerer
External products run as operator-installed programs in an operator-fixed mode
One steer operation with tree-scoped authority; waits read only the caller's inbox

Child routes come from a live host setting; persona and tools come from the preset
A team is the tree plus a task board in the root's log

The root's log says what ran, for whom and how it ended, also after a crash

Resuming a root closes each open run as interrupted once; a fork ignores inherited records

Concurrent sends, a release and a resume of one child are serialised and lose nothing
Capacity, depth and the start budget refuse a start and a cold resume; a live limit change applies to the next start
Name rule, default agent-N, duplicates refused, no shared name under concurrent starts

Send authority: outside the tree, self, external and dismissed targets refused; only a cold target is resumed
wait_agent ends on new or edited next-step input and on nothing else

Task compare-and-set: stale revision, cycle, unready claim and non-root reassign are refused

wait through the tool endpoint returns the bounded result, is cancellable, and records the calling agent as creator
A target with isolation: worktree starts its child in its own checkout and branch, is refused outside Git, cleans up on release and merges nothing

Stopping and killing the host leave no child and an honest ledger

A task runs in a second dsh process and in a real ACP agent
Claude Code and Codex, as installed, through one tool with two targets
